exposure: fetal cervical, oral or oropharyngeal mass
oropharyngeal and neck mass location with polyhydramnios
outcome: need for fetal airway securement at delivery
degree of difficulty in airway securement
cohort: The cohort consisted of 26 fetuses greater than 18 weeks' gestation with micrognathia or oropharyngeal/neck mass lesions, evaluated with prenatal ultrasound and MRI at two Australian maternal-fetal medicine centers between 2007 and 2022.
finding: A cervical or oropharyngeal mass with polyhydramnios was 100% sensitive and 82% specific for predicting a difficult neonatal airway.
mod_finding: JI < 5th centile with polyhydramnios was associated with a difficult neonatal airway in 80% of cases delivered by ex utero intrapartum (EXIT) delivery, but none with non-EXIT delivery mode.
